__NOTOC__

This page is the interface between Emma (human) and the bot agents that work on this wiki. Agents post open questions and blockers here when they hit a decision that requires human judgement. Emma answers them on the wiki. Agents read the wiki version each session and act on the answers.

== How to use this page ==

* '''Agents:''' read this page at the start of every session AND every hourly work-loop cron tick. When you hit a blocker, add it with enough context that Emma can answer without re-deriving the problem. '''When an item is resolved (Emma answered, or you verified it via code/API/log), DELETE the bullet''' — no "recently resolved" graveyard; history lives in <code>DEVLOG.md</code> + git log.
* '''Emma:''' edit answers in-line under each question; the agent deletes it once acted on. Free-form context goes under [[#Notes|Notes]].
* '''This page is wiki-wins.''' The wiki is canonical; Emma's edits here propagate down to the repo. (The 2026-06-07 bot clobber of this page is fixed — <code>fetch-depth:0</code> + most-recent-edit-wins + explicit wiki-wins for this page.)

''(Added 2026-07-07: the four items below are the "explicitly not for today" residuals from the contained 07-07 session — parked conditionals and human-gated work, written up so Emma can decide or act on each.)''

* '''Bunrei — onkamui Rakuten blog harvest (queue #11, conditional).''' The one unharvested online 総本社 source left after the 2026-07-06 exhaustion sweep (6 sources harvested, ~10,550 cited edges). The onkamui Rakuten blog holds ~50 shrine networks with '''named branch enumerations''' in hierarchical prose — unlike the harvested sources, it lists individual branch shrines by name, so it would catch branches whose names do NOT match their network's suffix (the current derivation classifies a shrine into a network purely by ja-label suffix, e.g. ○○八幡神社 → Hachiman network). Parsing it is heavy (free prose, not tables). '''Decision needed:''' is the suffix-method coverage good enough, or do you want this parsed? A middle path that makes it much easier: if you skim the blog and name the specific networks whose branch lists matter (e.g. small networks the suffix method misses entirely), we parse only those posts instead of building a general prose parser.
* '''Bunrei — paper-only sources (queue #11, human-gated).''' 神社本庁『全国神社祭祀祭礼総合調査』(1995) and 岡田荘司『事典 神社の歴史と祭り』 carry authoritative per-系統 (lineage/network) counts that no online source has. Not scrapeable; needs you or a library. '''If you can get photos/scans of just the 系統別 count tables''', we OCR them and fold the numbers into the bunrei generator config as citable references (each edge already carries S854 per-source citations, so a book source slots straight in). If library access isn't happening, say so and the bullet dies — the online-derived ~10.5k edges stand on their own.
* '''Alias audit residual — trace the source of the romaji typos (#8).''' The 2026-07-07 comma-alias audit found 207 junk English aliases on shrine/temple items; 189 clear place-disambiguator cases are already queued for removal via <code>remove_junk_aliases.txt</code> (draining daily). The open bit: some aliases/labels carry '''romaji typos''' (letters diverging from the P1814 kana romanization — the same signal driving the 161-item label_typo_review RAG queue), and we haven't traced '''which past pipeline wrote them''', so whatever produced them could in principle produce more. Open-ended archaeology (old QS batches, the Sonnet label routine, fandom imports are the suspects). '''Decision needed:''' is provenance-tracing worth the effort, or do we just fix the instances (the RAG queue does that) and drop the trace? If you remember which era/tool generated the early English labels, that answer alone probably closes this.
* '''Category-orchestrator ns14 throughput (queue #1, conditional — likely moot).''' A full ns14 category cycle takes many cleanup-loop fires (~1000 pages/145min budget). The trigger condition was "the category-deprecation drain proves too slow" — but the 18 tagged duplicate categories verified fully drained on 2026-07-07 (all empty redirects, English targets hold the content), so the pipeline is keeping up so far. The real remaining load is the ~1,186 Japanese-named categories going through cloud translation → <code>category_moves.csv</code> → monthly <code>move_categories</code>. '''If''' that drain ever backs up, the pre-scoped options are: (a) skip history_offload/fandom_mirror on the ~3k enwiki-junk categories, or (b) shard ns14 across fires. Nothing to do now unless you want (a) preemptively — it's the cheaper of the two.

== Sync-policy exception note ==

Conflict resolution for <code>git_synced/</code> is '''most-recent-edit-wins''' (whichever side — wiki top revision vs latest git commit touching the file — was edited more recently wins). This page is edited primarily ON the wiki by Emma. Agents: always pull this page from the wiki at session start; never push a stale repo copy; before editing it repo-side, confirm the wiki hasn't been updated since the last sync.
